95fc9ba43ec6ffc7: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan negeri bimbang kehilangan sumber kebergantungan sekiranya ahli majlis pihak berkuasa tempatan (PBT) dipilih melalui pilihan raya, kata Timbalan Presiden Muda, Zaidel Baharuddin.
Beliau berkata bantahan terhadap pilihan raya kerajaan tempatan melibatkan parti politik di kedua-dua belah pihak dan tidak lagi terhad kepada Barisan Nasional (BN) sahaja.
Berucap dalam satu forum politik, Zaidel berkata kerajaan negeri mempunyai kuasa percukaian yang terhad, manakala PBT menjana pendapatan melalui cukai taksiran harta, lesen dan fi lain.
PBT juga memainkan peranan penting dalam melaksanakan dasar kerajaan negeri, termasuk yang berkaitan dengan penggunaan tanah dan pembangunan.
Beliau berkata kerajaan negeri berdepan kekangan perlembagaan dan kewangan, menjadikan PBT sumber pendapatan yang penting serta instrumen untuk melaksanakan dasar kerajaan negeri.
“Masalahnya apabila datuk bandar tidak dipilih melalui pilihan raya ialah mereka tidak bertanggungjawab kepada anda,” katanya dalam sesi mengenai reformasi kerajaan tempatan.
Beliau mencadangkan supaya jawatan datuk bandar Kuala Lumpur dipilih secara pilihan raya sebagai projek perintis demokrasi tempatan.
Beliau berkata penduduk Kuala Lumpur kini boleh mengundi Ahli Parlimen, tetapi tidak mempunyai perwakilan di peringkat negeri, manakala pentadbiran bandar itu berada di bawah kerajaan Persekutuan.
“Lihat Kuala Lumpur bukan sebagai sebuah negeri, tetapi sebagai sebuah bandar,” katanya.
"Walaupun pilihan raya PBT tidak akan menghapuskan rasuah atau kegiatan melobi, persaingan pilihan raya boleh meningkatkan akauntabiliti dan tadbir urus."
Zaidel turut menolak kebimbangan bahawa pilihan raya kerajaan tempatan terlalu rumit untuk diadakan.

Beliau mencadangkan bahawa kelayakan pengundi boleh disahkan melalui resit cukai taksiran harta atau bil utiliti yang menunjukkan bahawa penyewa telah menetap di sesuatu kawasan selama dua hingga tiga tahun.
Beliau mengkritik sistem semasa yang menggunakan mesyuarat libat urus awam, dengan berkata penjadualan dan struktur mesyuarat tersebut menyukarkan penduduk yang bekerja untuk mengambil bahagian.
Katanya, pemilihan ahli majlis yang boleh menghadiri mesyuarat perancangan dan pengezonan secara berkala akan lebih berkesan.

Pensyarah kanan di institut dasar awam Universiti Malaya, Helmi Abu Yahya berkata kekurangan kemahuan politik dalam kalangan parti pemerintah merupakan halangan utama untuk mengembalikan pilihan raya kerajaan tempatan.
Beliau turut berkata Malaysia tidak mempunyai badan bebas khusus untuk memantau prestasi kerajaan tempatan dan memperjuangkan reformasi perbandaran.
Penyertaan masyarakat yang lebih meluas juga diperlukan, sambil merujuk kepada jumlah kehadiran orang awam yang rendah dalam sesi pendengaran mengenai draf Pelan Struktur Kuala Lumpur 2040.
“Apabila kehadiran orang awam hampir tidak wujud, pembuat keputusan tertinggi menganggap orang awam belum bersedia untuk demokrasi tempatan,” katanya.
Pilihan raya kerajaan tempatan diadakan dari 1956 hingga 1965 sebelum digantung, kemudian dimansuhkan setahun selepas itu.
Sebuah suruhanjaya diraja yang ditubuhkan pada 1965 mengesyorkan supaya pilihan raya kerajaan tempatan dikembalikan.
Bagaimanapun, kerajaan persekutuan memutuskan untuk tidak berbuat demikian dan menggubal Akta Kerajaan Tempatan 1976, yang secara berkesan menggantung pilihan raya kerajaan tempatan.
Undang-undang itu memberi kuasa kepada kerajaan negeri untuk melantik datuk bandar, yang dipertua dan ahli majlis, dan bukannya memilih mereka melalui pilihan raya oleh orang awam.
Pada 2008, Pulau Pinang dan Selangor yang dipimpin Pakatan Harapan cuba menghidupkan semula pilihan raya tersebut bagi memenuhi janji pilihan raya, tetapi usaha itu tidak berhasil.

Pada Februari 2024, Menteri Perumahan dan Kerajaan Tempatan, Nga Kor Ming berkata pilihan raya kerajaan tempatan bukan keutamaan kerana kementeriannya memberi tumpuan kepada bidang lain, seperti keselamatan jalan raya serta kebersihan tandas awam dan longkang.

ff0c5ff775e1f5d9: BANGKOK, Oct 17 — The artificial intelligence boom has been a key driver of global growth, but also poses economic risks should investment in the technology falter, experts and policymakers said this week at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

Propelled by spending on data centres and microchips, AI has helped cushion the economic shock of rising global energy prices caused by war in the Middle East, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said in a report on Tuesday.
The fund’s chief economist Silvana Tenreyro noted this week that global trade rose 8.3 per cent between 2023 and 2025 — a figure she said would be closer to 4.6 per cent without AI-related products.
“It is everywhere in the global economy,” Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said of AI yesterday.
“You see it in GDP. You see it in the stock market. You see it in the bond market... So it is here, and it’s just the beginning.”
But some top officials gathered in Bangkok this week cautioned against relying too heavily on AI investment.
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh called AI the “most consequential change” to the global economy in his lifetime, and said it had “a huge benefit”. Still, he warned the road ahead would be “bumpy”.

“The path from where we are to there is likely to be a very bumpy one, bumpy in our understanding of the technology, bumpy because we really don’t know what the market structure is going to be of these new technologies,” he said.
IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva similarly noted the AI boom’s boost to global growth, but she told AFP that any slowdown in the industry “would be felt across the world”.
“If there is loss of confidence and money runs away from AI, that can lead to financial stability risks,” Georgieva said.
An IMF report released this week projected that a decline in AI investment could reduce global GDP by 0.4 per cent by 2028.
“Weaker or less durable AI investments and profitability could be a shock that triggers a market correction,” the report said.
War and regulation
While AI investment and trade have softened the global economic impact of the Middle East war, economists at Moody’s Analytics have warned that if the conflict drags on it could “puncture” the boom.

They said higher energy prices and tighter financial conditions could push up operating costs and interest rates, adding to doubts over “the long-term profitability and viability of AI business models”.
“A drawn-out conflict would put serious strain on the economics behind AI investment,” the group said.
The uncertainty around regulation has also clouded the technology’s outlook.
Leaders like US President Donald Trump have urged more limited government regulation, even as some in the industry have called for legislation to mitigate risks.
Georgieva, the IMF chief, appeared yesterday to link such regulation to future investment.
“If there are no safeguards, then the risks may exceed the opportunities,” she said in Bangkok. — AFP
029477171de4bfa9: RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazil's right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said on Friday that he had not considered giving his father a government position in the event of victory, though he did not rule out the possibility.

Eduardo, 42, gave up his seat as a lawmaker in Brazil when he moved to the United States last year.
He was sentenced in absentia in June to four years and two months in prison after urging US sanctions on his country during his father's coup trial.
During the interview, Flavio Bolsonaro described the incumbent government as "chaos" and insisted that the "Lula era is about to end."
"There are only nine days left before the election, before we can turn this sad page of history," the senator said.
Bolsonaro finished ahead of Lula by 47% to 45% in the first round of voting on October 4.

Bolsonaro was on 51% of valid votes against Lula's 49%, within the survey's two-point margin of error.

2a550a751f635372: BEIJING: A member of a Chinese AI-generated girl group has sparked online backlash after announcing she was pregnant.
She said she would temporarily leave the group to rest and recover, prompting criticism that the creators were using women's real-life experiences as a publicity stunt.
Mity, also known as Kim Min-ti, is part of BABYQUEEN, a five-member virtual girl group styled after South Korean pop acts.
The group announced on the Chinese social media platform Xiaohongshu that Mity was "expecting a baby" and would take temporary maternity leave.
They added that her return would depend on her "physical condition".
The announcement asked fans to be understanding and send their blessings, while refraining from excessive speculation about the virtual idol's private life.
Mity subsequently posted an apology on the group's social media account, saying her personal circumstances had affected the group.
"I'd first like to apologise, as my personal issues have affected the group," she wrote, adding that she had "recently confirmed her pregnancy" and would take a break to "focus on resting".
The post quickly drew disbelief and ridicule online, with users questioning how an AI character could become pregnant.
One commenter asked: "What exactly does it even mean for an AI girl group member to be pregnant?"
Another joked: "Even AI has to get pregnant now? Human civilisation is doomed!"
The controversy worsened when BABYQUEEN released a teaser for a new song featuring its four remaining members just an hour after Mity's statement appeared.
The timing led people online to accuse the creators of using a fake pregnancy to drum up publicity for the new single.
Critics also argued that using pregnancy and childbirth as a dramatic plot point trivialised genuine female experiences.
Beyond the jokes, the backlash raised serious questions about ethics in AI entertainment and the trend of virtual idols fabricating realistic personal lives.
Amid the criticism, a creator behind the project admitted that the story was simply a way to reduce their workload.
"As I am unable to manage all these AI characters by myself, I thought of removing some of them," she explained. "That's why I chose this inappropriate reason to have Mity leave the group."
The creator, who mentioned she was a student, acknowledged that using a pregnancy as an excuse was a poor decision.

The team behind the group also spoke about the pressure of running the project, explaining that as students, they had not yet made any money from their work and were now facing online harassment and personal attacks.
The incident highlights the growing challenges for creators of virtual entertainers.

While AI idols can build fanbases and promote music or brands, BABYQUEEN's stunt has sparked a broader debate about whether fictional storylines cross an ethical line when they turn sensitive human experiences into marketing tools.

a033041a7be75c32: SINGAPORE, Oct 17 — Afternoon showers over parts of Singapore helped keep hourly PM2.5 from climbing into the very high band this afternoon.

The Denmark Open has historically been a disappointment for the pair, who were eliminated in the early rounds. This is only the second time Pearly-Thinaah have qualified for a World Tour Super 750 final, the last one being at the French Open in 2022.
Their final appearance at this championships strengthens their position on the qualifying list for the World Tour Finals in December where only the top eight are selected.
They are currently in the sixth spot and can expect to jump a slot or two after tomorrow.
3d4736d477d76ee1: KUALA LUMPUR: Scratch men's doubles pair Kang Khai Xing–Lok Hong Quan's gallant run at the Malaysia Super 100 ended in the semi-finals on Saturday.
The sixth seeds fell 21–15, 21–10 to South Korea's fifth seeds Jin Yong–Jo Song Hyun in 30 minutes at the Indoor Arena, EduCity Sports Complex, in Iskandar Puteri, Johor.
Their defeat ended Malaysia's challenge, making this the first edition without a Malaysian champion since the tournament began in 2023.

Playing their first tournament together, Khai Xing–Hong Quan were the only Malaysians to reach the last four after mixed doubles pair Liew Xun–Nicole Tan and women's pair Dania Sofea Zaidi–Tan Zhing Hui exited in the quarter-finals.
Malaysia claimed two titles at the inaugural edition in 2023 through Leong Jun Hao in men's singles and Chan Peng Soon–Cheah Yee See in mixed doubles.
The hosts secured another two crowns in 2024, with Low Hang Yee–Ng Eng Cheong winning the men's doubles and Go Pei Kee–Teoh Mei Xing taking the women's doubles.
Last year, Khai Xing partnered Aaron Tai to the men's doubles title, beating compatriots Chia Wei Jie–Lwi Sheng Hao in the final.
a151dc9fe2725178: KUALA LUMPUR: Heavy rain has prompted complaints from residents about recurring floods in parts of the Klang Valley, with one resident blaming clogged drains near an unfinished pedestrian walkway in Petaling Jaya.

In a post on Threads, user _anuarlatif said flooding frequently occurred in Taman Putra Damai, Lembah Subang, which the user attributed to blocked drains following construction work along the area's main road.
The user said soil and construction materials left by the roadside appeared to have washed into the drains, obstructing water flow.
"Can the minister look into the problems residents here face whenever it rains, causing floods in our neighbourhood?
"The pedestrian walkway has been left unfinished for a long time. The problem stems from the contractor building the walkway along the main road.
"When it rains, soil and materials fall into the drains, eventually blocking the water flow," the user said in a post today.
The Petaling Jaya City Council said the user should provide the full address of the affected area to facilitate checks and further action.
Meanwhile, another Threads user, amm.yusopp, reported flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang.
Further details on the flooding at both locations, including water levels and the impact on residents, were not available.
8dc8a5d939903405: CHENNAI, Oct 17 — Indian music composer Deva, hugely popular for his unique ‘gana’ style, died here today, Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
He was 75 and breathed his last at a private hospital here, sources said.

‘Gana’ songs, Deva’s gift to Tamil-speaking people, may be described as a genre of musical composition that brought the subaltern world into the mainstream, capturing its likes, dislikes, and the rough-and-tumble lives of youth.

In a career spanning nearly four decades, Deva composed music for over 400 films. These included runaway hits such as the Rajinikanth-starrers Annamalai (1992) and Baasha (1995), both directed by Suresh Krissna, alongside Kamal Haasan’s Pammal K Sambandam (2002) and Panchathanthiram, also released the same year.
Known for his stentorian voice, Deva sang a wide variety of songs himself.
Besides his hit songs, several of Deva’s background scores remain hits with moviegoers, including the pulsating Baasha, Baasha from the Rajinikanth-led blockbuster.
His score for veteran comedian Goundamani’s antics in the Tamil film Sooriyan (1992) remains vividly remembered by movie lovers.
Deva was known for his signature white pyjama-kurta and white sandals, with his choice of footwear reportedly inspired by Rajinikanth.
Deva’s son, Srikanth Deva, is also a well-known music director.
The film fraternity, Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, and various political leaders expressed profound grief over Deva’s demise. — Bernama-PTI
b98dd8352c4dddfd: KUALA LUMPUR: State governments fear a loss of reliance if local councils are elected, Muda deputy president Zaidel Baharuddin told a forum here today. He said opposition to local elections extended to political parties on both sides, and was no longer confined to Barisan Nasional.

Speaking at a workshop on politics here, Zaidel said state governments had limited powers of taxation, while local councils generated revenue through property assessment taxes, licences and other fees. They also played a key role in implementing state policies, including those related to land use and development.
He said state governments faced constitutional and financial constraints, making local councils important sources of revenue and instruments for implementing state policies.

“The problem when you have mayors who are not elected is that they are not answerable to you,” he said at a session on reform of local government. He proposed introducing a directly elected mayor for Kuala Lumpur as a pilot project for local democracy.
He said Kuala Lumpur residents could currently vote for members of Parliament, but lacked state-level representation, while the city’s administration fell under the federal government.

“Look at Kuala Lumpur not as a state, but as a city,” he said. Although local council elections would not eliminate corruption or lobbying, electoral competition could improve accountability and governance.

Zaidel also dismissed concerns that local elections would be too complicated to organise. He suggested that voter eligibility could be verified through property assessment receipts or utility bills showing two to three years of residence for tenants.

He criticised the current system of public town hall meetings, saying their scheduling and structure made participation difficult for working residents. Electing councillors who could regularly attend planning and zoning meetings would be more effective, he added.
Helmi Abu Yahya, a senior lecturer at Universiti Malaya's public policy institute, said a lack of political will among ruling parties was the main obstacle to restoring local council elections.

He also said Malaysia lacked dedicated independent bodies to monitor local government performance and advocate for municipal reform. Greater civic participation was also needed, pointing to low public turnout at hearings on the draft Kuala Lumpur Structure Plan 2040.
“When public turnout is virtually non-existent, top decision-makers view the public as unprepared for local democracy,” he said.

Local elections were held from 1956 to 1965 before being suspended, and then abolished a year later. A royal commission set up in 1965 called for local elections to be restored; however, the federal government decided against it and enacted the Local Government Act 1976, effectively suspending local elections.
The law empowers state governments to appoint mayors, presidents, and councillors, rather than having them elected by the public.
In 2008, the Pakatan Harapan-led states of Penang and Selangor attempted to revive the polls, to meet election promises, but to no avail.

In February 2024, housing and local government minister Nga Kor Ming said local council elections were not a priority as his ministry was focussing on other areas – such as road safety and cleaner public toilets and drains.
44e84b9497a21540: Late Sunday night, a still-unknown cybercriminal or group hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of French grocery stores, spiking temperatures, spoiling food, and sparking fires. This is part of an ongoing trend of attacking physical systems that can do damage in the real world. In August, a ransomware attack disrupted building-management systems at a Canadian hospital, affecting door access controls, central HVAC monitoring, and the issuing of staff access cards. And three years ago, cyberattacks hit Las Vegas casinos, causing slot machines to go dark, preventing payment kiosks and ATMs from spitting out cash, and locking guests out of their rooms when the electronic keys stopped working. Not all digital intrusions remain in cyberspace, and attackers don’t need to encrypt files and steal data to cause chaos. Hitting physical systems often produces more severe consequences - and turns up the heat on executives to pay an extortion demand. “There was one gig where the customer was refusing to pay, and so the threat actor was like, ‘Hold my beer, have fun getting into your offices,’ and locked everybody out,” Tim Beasley, a senior incident response consultant at Semperis, told The Register. Beasley won’t name the customer, or provide any incriminating information, but said the incident response involved police smashing glass in addition to his team recovering compromised data. “The cops had to break in, and literally get into the building, breaking some windows, so the customer was able to finally get back in,” he said. We asked if the customer paid the ransom demand, and Beasley yelled: “Oh, hell, no!” A report published earlier this month by ServiceNow’s Armis Labs found increasing evidence of ransomware attackers using physical consequences as leverage in their intrusions. “Today’s BAS operate at the intersection of IT and OT worlds, creating unprecedented exposure,” the report said. Ransomware with physical consequences Building automation systems - BAS - are the critical systems that control and monitor facilities’ HVAC, lighting, energy usage, and water consumption. They also oversee badge readers, door locks, surveillance cameras, fire alarm control panels, and other physical safety equipment. As such, BAS make very attractive targets for ransomware operators looking for high-pressure ways to extort organizations into paying multi-million ransom demands. These systems also appeal to government-backed goons and hacktivists looking to ensure maximum psychological and physical impact during destructive cyberattacks. Armis Labs found 73 percent of organizations own BAS that have been used in ransomware attacks, and this same percentage have known exploited vulnerabilities in at least one of their building automation systems. Additionally, 91 percent of BAS communicate over insecure protocols - opening up an even bigger attack surface for cyber-miscreants wanting to cause physical harm. “The primary thing that we see with any attack on building management systems or physical systems: It’s a great place for the threat actor to hide,” Michael Freeman, ServiceNow’s senior director of threat research, told The Register. “It's easier for them to compromise, and it's easier for them to hide in.” BAS and operational technology (OT) in general have fewer security controls than IT systems. Most require continual uptime, which makes them harder to patch or even scan for vulnerabilities and misconfigurations as this may lead to outages. “One case in particular, against a very large financial institution, the threat actors were staying low and quiet by attacking their BMS systems, and then pivoting into the IT environment,” Freeman said. The intruders were routinely caught - and booted from - the financial institution’s IT systems, so they built backdoors into the BMS to ensure persistent access to both OT and IT networks. “We're also seeing threat actors using AI to understand more building automation systems, especially ones that are using obscure OSs like VxWorks, older Unix-type systems,” Freeman said. AI has entered the chat As multiple security experts have told us in previous interviews, security through obscurity is dead. Not only does AI make it easier for attackers to find bugs – some very obscure and decades old - but it also means criminals no longer need to be OT experts to carry out destructive cyberattacks on critical networks and facilities. Instead, they can use AI to learn all about the obscure protocols and proprietary hardware and software that historically made industrial control systems black boxes. “It’s easier to understand what the controls are,” Freeman said, using the example of an attacker trying to take down a plane, or some similar catastrophic cyberattack. Historically, even advanced, government-backed hacking squads would “be quiet, because you don't know what changing certain settings is going to do,” Freeman explained. “Now you can use AI to say, ‘If I compromise a weight and balance system for airlines, all I need to do now is move this number here to this number, and I just told the system to load heavy stuff on the right side of the plane instead of equal distribution.'” Freeman told us he has seen attackers break into airlines’ OT gear in the past. “But they didn’t know what they were getting into, and so they left them alone,” he said. “Those do cause me concern because in the past I've helped to kick people out of those types of systems.” Industrial orgs increasingly under attack OT security provider Dragos tracks ransomware groups’ claims against industrial organizations on the criminals’ leak sites, along with publicly disclosed intrusions affecting manufacturing and other critical sectors. To be clear: claims on leak sites aren’t always accurate or even true, and the claim itself doesn’t mean operations or control systems were hit. Since 2022, however, “the numbers have been consistently increasing,” Lexie Mooney, senior threat analyst at Dragos, told The Register. The cybersecurity firm tracked 995 ransomware attacks against industrial orgs in 2023, a 49.5 percent increase from 2022. That number jumped more than 87 percent in 2024. Active ransomware groups targeting industrial orgs also grew in 2024 to 80 groups, up from 50 the year before. Dragos tracked 119 ransomware groups impacting more than 3,300 industrial organizations in 2025, and the incidents have steadily increased every quarter this year: 1,020 incidents in the first quarter of 2026 and 1,140 incidents in Q2. “The vast majority of cases are opportunistic,” Abdul Alamri, a senior threat analyst at Dragos, told us. “In some of the cases that we have seen an operational impact, either physical systems or an OT operation, it’s just the nature of the opportunism on the part of those ransomware groups.” This is partially due to the complexity of OT systems, he added. “Ransomware groups want to disrupt operations, and put pressure on the victims to pay the ransom,” Alamri said. “They don’t want to invest that time and effort to target complex systems." It’s usually quicker and easier for financially motivated crims to affect operations via IT systems - as the extortionists did in the August 2025 Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) breach, which halted manufacturing and crippled business operations for months. Internet-connected OT: the next 'low-hanging fruit' The other side of this complexity, however, is that many organizations themselves still lack visibility into their OT environments. Dragos estimates that fewer than 10 percent of OT networks worldwide currently have sufficient network monitoring in place. Plus, in 30 percent of incidents the security firm responded to in 2025, the investigations did not begin with a detection alert, but with someone noticing that “something seemed wrong” in operations. This lack of visibility, combined with threats from AI, worries Alamri. “If you compare the risk that we have seen from humans, to what we are about to face in the near future with AI agents who might continuously try to break into those systems - it’s a pretty dark future if we don't take the right measures to protect ourselves against it.” As organizations get better at patching and securing IT systems, attackers will likely look to internet-connected OT systems where digital compromises have real-world consequences, according to Matt Hayden, VP of cyber and emerging threats at General Dynamics Information Technology. “We all anticipate that as we get better at reducing the IT low-hanging fruit, OT will become a vector of much more scrutiny and much more attention,” Hayden told The Register. Before joining GDIT, Hayden served as the assistant secretary for cyber, infrastructure, risk and resilience policy at the US Department of Homeland Security. Compliance vs. security “There is a big focus on the hardware being connected for the purpose of compliance - and to make sure that, in the name of compliance, we aren't opening back doors, to devices that traditionally wouldn't have to be connected to facilitate their service,” he said, using refrigeration units as an example of one such system that is now internet-connected for compliance purposes. This was prior to the French supermarket hacks. Refrigeration units’ monitoring systems connect to the internet so their owners and operators can prove to regulators that the units maintain their uptime and temperature in accordance with regulations. “So if the health department comes by, they say, ‘Look, my refrigerator was at 27 degrees for the last 72 days,' and they have a check mark, and they get their A plus. But that simple connectivity is also a vector in which that particular refrigerant unit could be targeted for disruption,” Hayden said. About a week after our interview, criminals did exactly that. “The recently reported exploitations of commercial refrigeration units represent a significant example of devices without digital value, no sensitive data or extended enterprise access, being exploited by being connected to the internet with unpatched firmware,” Hayden told us in a subsequent email. He said he expects the attribution to be “less nation-state, and more likely those looking for targets of opportunity to identify what could be done with the unpatched systems.” “The consequences are food supply degradation at a small scale, but it is an important example of what could happen at scale very quickly with more consequential operating equipment,” Hayden said.®
09cc9cf3efc0bac4: RIO DE JANEIRO, Oct 17 — Brazil’s right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said yesterday that he had not considered giving his father a government position in the event of victory, though he did not rule out the possibility.
Bolsonaro will face leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on October 25 in the country’s presidential election runoff.
Former president Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio’s father, is currently under house arrest for planning a coup after losing the 2022 presidential election to Lula.
“He has never suggested that he would like to work in the government... he has never raised the subject with me, so it’s not on the radar,” Flavio Bolsonaro said in an interview with TV Globo.
He did not close the door on the possibility of his father’s involvement in government should he win, though the 45-year-old ruled out appointing his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro as foreign minister.
Eduardo, 42, gave up his seat as a lawmaker in Brazil when he moved to the United States last year.
He was sentenced in absentia in June to four years and two months in prison after urging US sanctions on his country during his father’s coup trial.
During the interview, Flavio Bolsonaro described the incumbent government as “chaos” and insisted that the “Lula era is about to end.”
“There are only nine days left before the election, before we can turn this sad page of history,” the senator said.
Bolsonaro finished ahead of Lula by 47 per cent to 45 per cent in the first round of voting on October 4.
A Datafolha poll published on Thursday showed his lead in the runoff narrowing from four per centage points to two, putting the rivals in a statistical tie.
Bolsonaro was on 51 per cent of valid votes against Lula’s 49 per cent, within the survey’s two-point margin of error. — AFP
9dafb5c002d4e76e: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — The Madani Government has increased the allocation for religious affairs to RM3.1 billion under Budget 2027 to strengthen Islamic development, including support for religious education institutions and the welfare of religious personnel nationwide.

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said 85.4 per cent of the allocation was for operating expenditure, while the remaining 14.6 per cent was set aside for development expenditure.
He said the increase reflected the government’s commitment to a more comprehensive agenda to elevate the stature of Islam and benefit society.

“The Madani Government continues to place special emphasis on this agenda by allocating RM200 million for sekolah agama rakyat (community religious schools), tahfiz institutions and sekolah pondok (traditional Islamic boarding schools) registered with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).
“The scope of assistance has also been expanded to cover the operating costs of these institutions,” he said in a statement here today.

Zulkifli said the government would also provide a special contribution of RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel, including Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain (Kafa) teachers, takmir teachers, imams, bilals, tok siaks, nojas and marbuts, in recognition of their contributions to the community.
He said 500 Kafa teachers who taught students with special needs, including those who used sign language or the Braille Quran, would receive a special monthly incentive of RM150.

“The well-being of those who enliven the Houses of Allah is further supported by a special government allocation that fully covers Social Security Organisation contributions for 40,000 imams, bilals, tok siaks, mosque staff and takmir teachers.

“The Pilgrims Fund Board (Tabung Haji) serves as the implementing agency, ensuring continuous social security protection and providing peace of mind to these individuals as they serve the ummah,” he said.

In a related development, Zulkifli said amendments to the Road Transport Act requiring drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs to compensate victims or their families contained elements consistent with the Islamic legal concept of diyat, or financial compensation.
He said the concept recognised the right of victims or their heirs to receive compensation for harm caused by another person’s actions.

Zulkifli said the government was also strengthening the halal industry by offering matching grants of up to RM5,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking halal certification for the first time.
A separate grant of RM25,000 would be available to empower halal-certified MSMEs in high-potential sectors, including cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, he added.

In the Islamic education sector, he said Jakim and the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) had initiated a collaboration to provide digital devices and skills training to teachers and students at more than 300 pondok schools nationwide.

Zulkifli said the initiatives reflected the government’s approach of focusing not only on economic and infrastructure development but also on nurturing a knowledgeable, ethical and prosperous society.
“This Budget 2027 framework is formulated based on a philosophy that aspires to reach for the skies while remaining firmly rooted on the ground.
“We aim to elevate the nation’s economy and the stature of Islam to the pinnacle of success, guided by a far-sighted vision,” he said.
He added that the government’s priorities and policy implementation would remain grounded in reality, with the ultimate aim of safeguarding the welfare and well-being of Malaysians. — Bernama

* Editor’s note: Jakim is the abbreviation for Jabatan Kemajuan Islam Malaysia in Malay, or the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia in English. Tahfiz refers to the memorisation of the Quran and, in this context, institutions dedicated to teaching it. Takmir refers to religious classes or activities organised to enliven and strengthen mosque life. Kafa stands for Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain, or Quran and Fardu Ain classes that teach children Quran recitation and memorisation, as well as basic Islamic religious obligations and practices. Bilal refers to a mosque official who assists the imam and calls Muslims to prayer. Tok siak refers to a mosque caretaker or attendant. Noja (plural: nojas) refers to a person responsible for maintaining a mosque and assisting with its daily operations. Marbut refers to a mosque caretaker or person responsible for its upkeep.
a7a51395f63cc055: SHANGHAI, Oct 17 — Top seed Alexander Zverev fell to a relentless Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the Shanghai Masters semi-finals today over three tense sets.
Davidovich Fokina, ranked 26th, fought back to win 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 and will play either Daniil Medvedev or fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar in the final tomorrow.
The 27-year-old Spaniard combined grit, lightning-fast returns and graceful drop shots to stun the German, who will end the year world number one.
“I was a little bit nervous,” Davidovich Fokina told the crowd afterwards of his shaky start.
“But I keep going, I keep fighting, every ball,” he said.
With his semi-final victory the Spaniard extended his winning streak in China to nine matches, after claiming an ATP 250 title in Chengdu.
The duo fought over long rallies in the first set, earning Davidovich Fokina a high-five from the world number two after one particularly impressive lob.
Despite a series of misjudged shots Zverev managed to avoid facing any break points in the first set.
He sprinted to send a brilliant backhand down the line, converting a crucial break point to go up 6-5.
He took the first set with an ace and looked to be heading back to the final he last reached in 2019.
Trouble arrived in the second set though as Zverev looked to be moving with some difficulty.
Davidovich Fokina worked his first break point in the fourth game but Zverev held when the Spaniard returned into the net.
Davidovich Fokina’s growing pressure paid off and he successfully ran for a backhand to take the match into a deciding set.
The emboldened Spaniard raced into a 3-0 lead.
The German saved two match points but the reprieve was only a brief one. — AFP
3c85e77354ec4709: CAIRO: Egyptian president Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that he would not seek to remain in office when his current term expires in 2030, describing the matter as "completely settled".

Sisi, 71, a former army general who became president in 2014, made the remarks at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy in the New Administrative Capital, one of his flagship megaprojects.
Speaking to graduates and state officials in the sprawling new city east of Cairo, Sisi said the Egyptian constitution "would not be touched".
"The period leading up to 2030 will be the end of my term as president of the state, if I am still alive. This is completely settled, and there will be no discussion about it," he said.
The Egyptian constitution, approved in 2014 following the 2013 military ouster of late Islamist president Mohamed Morsi, originally limited presidents to two four-year terms.
Constitutional amendments approved in a 2019 referendum extended presidential terms from four to six years and included transitional provisions that allowed Sisi to run for an additional term.
Under those amendments, Sisi was re-elected in 2023 for a six-year term that is due to expire in 2030.
Critics and opposition figures have speculated about the possibility of further constitutional changes that could allow him to remain in office beyond 2030.
Before running for president, Sisi denied having political ambitions, but he resigned from his position as defence minister in 2014 and entered the race he went on to win.

On Saturday, he said the run-up to 2030 would be used to groom a new generation of leaders, with the Military Academy training hundreds of prospective officials, ministers and presidential candidates in statecraft and leadership.

During his 12 years in power, Sisi has overseen an ambitious state-led development programme centred on megaprojects which critics say have relied heavily on borrowing and contributed to Egypt's mounting debt burden and economic pressures.

Sisi's presidency has also faced sustained criticism from international human rights organisations over restrictions on political opposition, civil society and freedom of expression, allegations the government rejects, saying its policies are necessary to preserve stability and security.
381bebdc7851f15d: KUALA LUMPUR: Mixed doubles pair Hoo Pang Ron–Lai Pei Jing know they need more than good shots to beat the world's best after their Denmark Open run was halted in the semi-finals on Saturday.
Consistency and patience remain the missing ingredients after the world No. 51 lost 21-13, 21-13 to China's world No. 1 Feng Yan Zhe–Huang Dong Ping at the SJF Bank Arena on Saturday.
The defeat ended their hopes of avenging last month's China Masters final loss to the same pair.
Pang Ron said producing quality shots was only part of the challenge against opponents who could respond with something better.
"Even when we played some good shots, they returned them better. After that, we needed to be more consistent and more patient," said Pang Ron.
The Malaysians had prepared for Denmark's different conditions, but Pang Ron admitted the Chinese pair adjusted their approach faster.
"It was different from the China Masters because the shuttles and the drift were different," he said.
"We prepared, but they were even more prepared and changed their game very quickly.
"We are still learning how to overcome each problem and respond faster."
Despite missing out on the final, Pei Jing said their performances throughout the tournament gave them reason to be encouraged.
"Overall, we are quite satisfied with our performance here because we improved from the first match until the semi-finals," she said.
"Although we are not going to the final, we are still very proud of this result."
Asked which aspect of their game had improved most, Pei Jing pointed to their mentality.
"We are getting there, slowly but surely," she added.
Pang Ron–Pei Jing will next compete in France before heading to Germany for the Hylo Open as they navigate a demanding tournament schedule.

a73522a3fefcaa29: Close to 1 billion meetings take place each day around the world. CEOs spend nearly three-quarters of their workdays in meetings. Planning for and spearheading meetings eats up the lion’s share of managers’ time. In much of the industrialized world, meetings are both the metronomes and menaces of people’s working lives.

Given the enormous time spent in workplace meetings, do we know what they accomplish or how to make them as worthwhile as possible? For decades, the answer was… not really. Meetings weren’t a particularly accessible subject of study. But that has changed. Once a tiny niche area, “meeting science” is a growing specialization among organizational and social psychologists. The field is accelerating as archived virtual meetings provide vast swaths of data. And it is providing a fascinating window into human behavior.

Meeting to talk helps fulfill basic human needs to connect, communicate, and cooperate. People have long come together—in caves, fields, market squares, and town halls—to get something done, share ideas, get on the same page, or just to remark on the weather. But meeting scientists define their subject as gatherings of people “with some goal or structure to the event,” says organizational psychologist Liana Kreamer of the Florida Institute of Technology, who coauthored a review of over three decades of meeting science in the 2026 Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior.
152d35195b8d4020: YANGON: A military airstrike on a village in central Myanmar killed 11 people, a rebel fighter said on Saturday.
Myanmar has been consumed by a civil war since a 2021 military coup ousted the elected government of Nobel Peace Prize laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.

The attack took place in territory controlled by the People's Defence Forces (PDF) rebel group in Yesagyo township, southwest of Mandalay city, at around 2.00pm (0730 GMT) on Friday, Bo Paw, a PDF member, said.
The attack killed 11 people, including six women and two children, among them a one-year-old who "could just walk a little bit", Bo Paw said.
The military could not be reached for comment.
A witness, who did not give his name for security reasons, described the aftermath of the attack.
"I saw three houses which were totally destroyed," he said. "These houses were at the roadside where the bomb hit."
"They all were killed on the spot, including an 11-year-old student who was riding a bicycle," he said.
More than 100,000 people have been killed in Myanmar since the start of the civil war, according to conflict monitor ACLED.
The PDF rose up around that time, alongside ethnic minority armies that have long resisted central rule.
However, after making significant gains against the military, the PDF forces find themselves on the back foot around Mandalay, Myanmar’s second-largest city.
da68b0a311b8f8ee: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Squash Racquets Association of Malaysia (SRAM) will focus on strengthening the preparations of national squash players in their mission to hunt for a gold medal at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games (LA28).
Its new president, Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin Tuanku Muhriz, said squash’s historic debut at the Olympic Games opens up a huge opportunity for Malaysia to make history at the prestigious sporting event.
He stated that SRAM’s new leadership will ensure that all needs, including support for the players, are given close attention to help them achieve their best performance ahead of LA28.
“I think the important thing now is the road to Olympics because squash for the first time is an Olympic sport. So, we have the opportunity to get a medal.
“So, I will combine a movement to really focus on the road to gold,” he told members of the media when met after SRAM’s 54th Annual General Meeting at the Malaysian Badminton Academy here today.
Earlier, Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin won uncontested for the presidency during the national governing body’s elections.
Also winning uncontested were former national squash player Azlan Iskandar for the deputy president post, Sharon Wee (vice-president), and Ramlee Abdullah (honorary treasurer).
Meanwhile, Nik Razeen Adam Daud was appointed as honorary secretary by the president, while Margaret Kechendai, Wan Sazril Wan Zaid, and Conrad Louis were elected as SRAM ordinary committee members.

Commenting on the pressure facing national squash, which is seen as one of the medal prospects for LA28, Tunku Zain acknowledged that there are high expectations on national players to realize that dream.
However, he said SRAM’s leadership responsibility is to ensure the athletes’ journey towards the games is facilitated through the provision of an effective support system.

“I think the pressure is on the players, not me. But as committee members, we will, of course, want to facilitate that journey so that they really can reach that dream because it’s a dream not just for squash players, but for all Malaysians,” he said.
Meanwhile, Tunku Zain said he does not plan to make major changes to SRAM’s existing structure, but rather wants to continue the successes and efforts implemented by the previous leadership.
He said squash has proven its position as one of Malaysia’s most successful sports based on its achievements in medals and championships at the international level.

At the same time, he wants to strengthen cooperation with state squash associations to ensure that the development of new talent continues and the country does not run out of quality players in the future.

According to him, building a broad participation base at the grassroots level is important to ensure that the continuity of national squash excellence does not halt when top players end their respective careers.
“If we see, there are other sports that might have been at the elite level at one time. But if there is no pipeline, we lose that continuity.
“So, insya-Allah, that’s what I want to focus on — cooperation with the state level so that the national level always has talent,” he said. — Bernama
96fe9d78bf736ec1: PETALING JAYA: Jabatan Imigresen Kuala Lumpur menyiasat bagi menentukan kesahihan dakwaan berlakunya penyelewengan dalam urusan pengeluaran pas khas di pejabat jabatan itu di Kuala Lumpur.
Pengarah Imigresen Kuala Lumpur, Hamsha Injau berkata siasatan akan dijalankan bahagian integriti dan pihaknya tidak akan berkompromi terhadap sebarang salah laku.
“Tindakan sewajarnya akan diambil sekiranya terdapat bukti pelanggaran undang-undang atau peraturan," katanya dalam kenyataan, lapor Bernama.
Hamsha juga menasihatkan orang ramai untuk berurusan melalui saluran rasmi Jabatan Imigresen dan tidak menggunakan khidmat orang tengah yang tidak diberikan kuasa.

Terdahulu hari ini, sebuah portal berita melaporkan dakwaan kemudahan pas khas yang sepatutnya membantu warga asing berdepan hal kecemasan dan mendesak dipercayai disalahgunakan secara sistematik untuk melanjutkan tempoh keberadaan mereka di Malaysia.

Laporan itu turut mendakwa kegiatan berkenaan melibatkan orang tengah tempatan yang menguruskan permohonan, mengumpul pasport pemohon dan menghantar gambar mereka kepada pegawai imigresen melalui aplikasi pesanan untuk pengesahan awal.
d193cb6106d6f2d1: MACHANG: After years of carrying a damaged identity card that was barely legible, 70-year-old Minah Yacob was relieved to receive her new-generation MyKad.

The Pangkal Payong resident received the card from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail during the Home Ministry's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambu Lawar here today.
Handing Minah the card, Saifuddin said: "Congratulations. Here is your new identity card."
Minah said her old identity card had been damaged for several years and was almost falling apart, making the information on it difficult to read.
The mother of six, who earns a living making and selling kuih, said receiving the new card had brought her considerable relief.
"I am very happy and relieved to finally have a new MyKad.
"My old identity card had been badly damaged for years, and the information on it could hardly be read," she said.
The New Generation MyKad is a version of the national identity card introduced by the National Registration Department, with improvements to its design, security features and functions.
It was issued in phases beginning Sept 17
cb0dd0bcd1b98ca7: ALOR GAJAH: Some 1.2 million workers who had previously opted not to contribute to the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam scheme have been urged to take up the protection following the announcement of an additional annual tax relief of RM150 under the 2027 Budget.

Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the incentive offered workers a good opportunity to resume contributions to ensure they had social security protection in the event of accidents outside working hours.
He said the importance of such protection was underscored by the 10,424 claims recorded under the scheme from June 1 to Sept 30, equivalent to an average of 85 cases a day.

"These figures remind us that accidents can happen at any time and that financial protection is crucial when someone faces adversity," he told reporters after launching the i Lindung u Gegar @ Melaka programme at Dataran Keris today.
He said the government understood public concerns over disposable income amid inflationary pressures driven by global factors, but social security protection must remain a priority.

Ramanan said the proposed Traveller Scheme for 480,000 Malaysians who travel daily to Singapore would be tabled in Parliament during the current sitting and implemented as promised by the prime minister when he announced it on Labour Day.

He also urged gig economy platform providers to utilise the RM30 million 2027 Budget allocation under the Lindung Kendiri scheme by co-funding contributions, which would boost the matching social security rate from 35 percent to 50 percent for gig workers earning RM3,000 or less.

"We also want to remind platform providers that enforcement to ensure compliance with Perkeso contributions began on Oct 1, including the obligation to make mandatory contribution deductions and integrate their respective systems with Perkeso's system," he said.

Meanwhile, the first i Lindung u Gegar @ Melaka programme held in the state targets 15,000 visitors as part of efforts by the Human Resources Ministry and Perkeso to bring government services closer to the public.
At the same programme, 400 housewives in Melaka were registered as Lindung Kasih contributors, making them eligible for Perkeso protection in the event of unforeseen mishaps.

dc01b1847cbecc8d: Neverwinter Nights was made by the studio that produced seminal RPGs Baldur's Gate, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, and Dragon Age. It sold well and was critically acclaimed at launch. Yet, somehow, it has not been canonized in most gamers' minds over the decades the same way the games that came before and after it were.

0406b6a0732b8116: WASHINGTON, Oct 17 — US President Donald Trump on Friday told supporters about his alleged attempt to have an ocean named after him and Google’s refusal to go along with the idea, reported German news agency dpa.

Speaking at a campaign rally in the state of Georgia, Trump claimed he had suggested to representatives of the internet giant that either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean be renamed the “Trump Ocean.” According to Trump, they responded indignantly: “We’ve had it. That’s enough. We’re not doing any more.”

Trump had already renamed the Gulf of Mexico the “Gulf of America” by executive order in 2025, followed by Lake Ontario on the Canadian border, which he renamed “Lake America” in August this year. Google Maps adopted both changes for users in the United States.
Trump told supporters he had sent Google a map labelled “Trump Ocean,” but company representatives rejected the idea.
“Sir, look, okay, this one we can’t do. Oceans are different. Oceans cover many, many countries. We can’t do it,” Trump quoted them as saying.
Trump said he had only been joking — this time — but added that it was not the worst idea he had ever had.
It was not immediately clear whether the exchange with Google had actually taken place.

Trump has repeatedly suggested that he would like to rename an ocean. He has also floated the idea of renaming the Strait of Hormuz the “Trump Strait,” apparently in an attempt to provoke Iran, with which the US is at war. — Bernama-dpa
af56e3154ddb1e4e: SEOUL: South Korean actress Kim Ji-won's comeback drama, Doctor X: Mafia in White, has sparked criticism over medical blunders, despite breaking viewing records just days after its release.
The SBS medical drama premiered on Oct 9 with a nationwide rating of 11.4 per cent, before jumping to 14.9 per cent for its second episode the next evening, according to Nielsen Korea.
The opening episode scored the highest debut rating for any South Korean miniseries in 2026.
Kim, 33, plays Gye Soo-jung, a brilliant but rebellious surgeon who takes on corrupt hospital bosses.
The series marks her return to television following the massive global success of Queen of Tears in 2024, where she starred alongside Kim Soo-hyun.
But viewers have questioned how realistic several medical scenes actually are.

One controversial scene features a patient with an inguinal hernia, leaving critics puzzled as to why emergency surgery was suddenly needed after the issue had already been fixed without an operation.
Others pointed out scenes where a surgeon calls the shots alone during complex operations that require multiple specialist doctors.
Some argued that the show completely ignores standard hospital procedures, especially in emergency care.
But fans defended the series, arguing that dramatic exaggeration is normal in fictional medical shows.
The debate grew stronger after emergency medicine doctor Namgung In, who worked as an on-set medical consultant, responded on social media on Oct 11.
"If you see something medically inaccurate, you can assume that the consultant and the production team disagreed, and the consultant lost the argument," he wrote.
Namgung also shared his appreciation for the production process, noting that it was his first time working as an on-set consultant.
Despite the debate over accuracy, he voiced his support for the show, praising the cast and crew's hard work and wishing it every success.

Adapted from the hit Japanese drama Doctor-X: Surgeon Michiko Daimon—which ran for seven seasons between 2012 and 2021—the Korean remake takes a darker, crime-thriller twist on the story of a rogue doctor fighting the medical system.
The new series is currently streaming on Netflix.
b44c0c7dccae721a: KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur immigration department will investigate allegations of irregularities in the issuance of special passes at its office.
Kuala Lumpur immigration director Hamsha Injau said the department's integrity division would conduct an investigation to determine if the allegations were true, and no misconduct would be tolerated.
“Appropriate action will be taken if there is evidence of any breach of the law or regulations,” he said in a statement.
He advised the public to deal with the department through official channels and avoid using unauthorised intermediaries.

A news portal reported today that special passes, which were intended to assist foreign nationals facing emergencies or urgent circumstances, were allegedly being systematically abused to extend their stay in Malaysia.

The report also alleged that the operation involved local intermediaries who handled applications, collected applicants' passports, and sent their photographs to immigration officers through messaging applications for preliminary verification.
8d63d933f7859a14: PUTRAJAYA: The Madani government has increased the allocation for religious affairs to RM3.1 billion under the 2027 Budget to strengthen Islamic development, including the empowerment of religious educational institutions and safeguarding the welfare of religious personnel nationwide.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said 85.4 per cent of the allocation was for operating expenditure, while the remaining 14.6 per cent was set aside for development expenditure.
He said the increase reflected the government's commitment to implementing a more comprehensive agenda to elevate the stature of Islam and benefit society.

"The Madani government continues to place special emphasis on this agenda by allocating RM200 million for sekolah agama rakyat (community religious schools), tahfiz institutions and sekolah pondok (traditional Islamic boarding schools) registered with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).
"The scope of assistance has also been expanded to cover the operating costs of these institutions," he said in a statement today.

Zulkifli said the government would also provide a special contribution of RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel, including Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain (KAFA) teachers, takmir teachers, imams, bilals, tok siaks, nojas and marbuts, in recognition of their contributions to the community.
He said 500 KAFA teachers who teach students with special needs, including those who use sign language or the Braille Quran, would receive a special monthly incentive of RM150.

"The well-being of those who enliven the Houses of Allah is further supported by a special government allocation that fully covers Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for 40,000 imam, bilal, tok siak, mosque staff and takmir teachers.

"The Pilgrims Fund Board (Tabung Haji) serves as the implementing agency, ensuring continuous social security protection and providing peace of mind to these individuals as they serve the ummah," he said.

In a related development, Zulkifli said amendments to the Road Transport Act requiring drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs to compensate victims or their families contained elements consistent with the Islamic legal concept of diyat, or financial compensation.
He said the concept recognised the right of victims or their heirs to receive compensation for harm caused by another person's actions.

He said the government was also strengthening the halal industry by offering matching grants of up to RM5,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking halal certification for the first time.
A separate grant of RM25,000 would be available to empower halal-certified MSMEs in high-potential sectors, including cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, he added.

In the Islamic education sector, he said Jakim and the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) had initiated a collaboration to provide digital devices and skills training to teachers and students at more than 300 pondok schools nationwide.

Zulkifli said the initiatives reflected the government's approach of focusing not only on economic and infrastructure development but also on nurturing a knowledgeable, ethical and prosperous society.

"This Budget framework is formulated based on a philosophy that aspires to reach for the skies while remaining firmly rooted on the ground. We aim to elevate the nation's economy and the stature of Islam to the pinnacle of success, guided by a far-sighted vision," he said.
He added that the government's priorities and policy implementation would remain grounded in reality, with the ultimate aim of safeguarding the welfare and well-being of Malaysians.
TAGS: Zulkifli Hasan, Budget 2027, Islamic teachings, education, welfare
